job.title: Senior HR Business Partner/ Org Design Lead
job.description:
The Company

Our client is a leading Australian organisation with a significant national presence across the aged care and community services sector. With a strong reputation for delivering high-quality care and services, the organisation is committed to making a meaningful difference in the lives of the communities it supports.

Following a significant acquisition, the business has entered an exciting period of transformation, expanding its national footprint and bringing together operations across multiple states. With this growth comes an opportunity to strengthen organisational structures, improve operational efficiencies and establish a more streamlined and sustainable operating model.

As Senior HR Business Partner, you will play a pivotal role in bringing this transformation to life, leading the implementation of a significant organisational restructure that will shape the future of the business.

The Leaders

Reporting directly to the CPO, you will work closely with the Executive Leadership Team and senior operational leaders, providing trusted HR advice and practical guidance throughout a complex period of organisational change.
This is an opportunity to work alongside an experienced leadership team who will value your expertise, judgement and ability to independently drive meaningful outcomes.

The Opportunity 

You will take ownership of the end-to-end implementation of a significant organisational restructure across a complex, multi-state business. With the overarching operating model and future-state organisational design already established, your focus will be on translating these plans into practical, sustainable structures, ensuring the right roles, reporting lines and accountabilities are in place to support the organisation's future.

This is a highly hands-on business partnering opportunity, requiring someone who can confidently advise senior executives while personally driving the detailed work behind the transformation. You will play an instrumental role in navigating sensitive workforce changes, balancing commercial objectives with a thoughtful, fair and compliant approach to employees.

You will have the opportunity to take ownership of:
  • Leading the end-to-end implementation of a significant organisational restructure, translating agreed operating models into detailed organisational structures, workforce plans and practical implementation activities.
  • Reviewing and refining organisational structures, reporting lines, spans of control and role accountabilities, identifying duplication, efficiencies and opportunities for improvement.
  • Leading detailed position mapping, role evaluation and the development of position descriptions to support the future organisational structure.
  • Developing and delivering comprehensive change and consultation plans, including employee communications, consultation documentation and supporting materials.
  • Managing complex workforce transition processes, including role selection, placement, redeployment and redundancies, ensuring compliance with relevant employment legislation and industrial instruments.
  • Partnering with Executive Leaders to provide strategic and operational HR advice on workforce decisions, organisational change and sensitive employee matters, coaching leaders through challenging conversations.
  • Working closely with Finance and Payroll to support workforce costing, headcount modelling, financial tracking and the delivery of targeted operational efficiencies.
  • Coordinating multiple workstreams and stakeholders, ensuring key milestones, risks and dependencies are effectively managed throughout the restructure.
  • Supporting the transition into the new organisational structure, ensuring changes are embedded effectively across people processes, systems and reporting arrangements.
About You

You will bring extensive experience as a Senior HR Business Partner or senior HR generalist, with strong capability across organisational change, employee relations and workforce restructuring. You will have a proven track record of personally leading and implementing significant organisational restructures within complex business environments.

You will have strong knowledge of Australian employment legislation, employee and industrial relations, and experience navigating complex workforce environments involving multiple stakeholders, employment arrangements and industrial instruments.

Importantly, you will have demonstrated experience taking organisational change beyond the strategic design phase, with the ability to independently manage detailed implementation activities, formal employee consultation, workforce transitions and redundancy processes. Exposure to large corporate, financial services, telecommunications, healthcare or similarly complex organisations will be highly regarded.

Above all, you will be a confident and credible HR Business Partner who can influence senior executives, navigate sensitive conversations and bring a pragmatic, solutions-focused approach to complex challenges.
This opportunity will suit someone who enjoys rolling up their sleeves, taking ownership and seeing meaningful transformation through from planning to implementation.

The Process

Including an initial consultation with a Levyl consultant, the interview process will involve meeting with key stakeholders to further explore your experience, approach to organisational restructuring and alignment with the organisation.

For further information or a confidential conversation, please contact Emilia Rodriguez on 0497938177.

Levyl encourages diverse, equitable and inclusive recruitment solutions and commits to responding to every applicant. We make selection and shortlist decisions based on your skills, experience, personal attributes and motivators.
When you apply for one of our roles, please tell us the pronouns you use and any reasonable adjustments you may need throughout the interview process.

job.title: HR Business Partner 12 Month FTC! $210K - $230K Package
job.description:
The Organisation

Levyl is partnering with a large, complex and geographically dispersed organisation to appoint a HRBP for a 12 month period, in a remote capacity! 

The organisation is progressing through a significant transformation program involving changes to its workforce, and operating structure. Consultation is already underway across multiple business areas, creating the need for additional business partnering capability during a critical period of change.

This is an opportunity to contribute to a meaningful and complex transformation program while working closely with senior leaders and an experienced People & Culture function.

The Team

Reporting to the Head of People Business Partners, you will join an established team of approximately six Business Partners located across NSW.

The team is experienced, collaborative and accustomed to working within a complex industrial environment. While each Business Partner is responsible for a designated portfolio, the team regularly shares knowledge, works through issues together and provides support across business areas when required.

You will be trusted to manage your portfolio with autonomy while remaining closely connected to the wider team through regular meetings and ongoing collaboration.

The Opportunity

As a People & Culture Business Partner, you will take ownership of a designated business portfolio and work closely with executives, senior leaders and employees.

The role will combine significant organisational change activity with broader operational business partnering. A key focus will be guiding leaders through workforce consultation, and union engagement while ensuring agreed activity continues to progress in line with the appropriate obligations and timeframes.

Your role will be to guide, coach and support leaders through the required processes while carefully managing the impact on employees.
Specific responsibilities will include:
  • Supporting leaders through organisational change, consultation and workforce realignment
  • Managing union engagement and formal consultation requirements
  • Interpreting and applying Enterprise Agreement provisions and relevant industrial instruments
  • Coaching leaders through sensitive decisions and challenging conversations
  • Ensuring agreed change activity progresses effectively and within required timeframes
  • Managing employee relations matters, complaints and workplace investigations as required
  • Providing advice across performance, workforce planning and organisational design
  • Supporting general People & Culture queries and day-to-day business partnering matters
  • Collaborating with employee relations and other specialist People & Culture teams
The opportunity is open to candidates located across NSW, with some planned travel potentially required depending on business needs, but mostly you will work remotely. 

About You

Levyl is looking for accomplished People & Culture Business Partners who can quickly understand a complex operating environment, establish credibility and provide confident support with minimal direction within a unionised environment.

You will bring substantial end-to-end business partnering experience, including direct involvement in organisational change, workforce consultation and industrial relations. Experience working with unions and independently interpreting Enterprise Agreements is essential.

Experience gained within utilities, infrastructure, government, local council, manufacturing or another operational and highly unionised environment will be highly regarded. Industry experience is less important than demonstrated success supporting complex change within an Enterprise Agreement-covered workforce. Along with this, a practical and proactive working style will be critical! You will know which questions to ask, where to find the information you need and when to bring the right people together to progress an issue.

The Process

This opportunity is being managed confidentially by Levyl. The interview process will include an initial meeting with a Levyl team member, followed by one or two meetings with the organisation’s senior People & Culture leaders.
For a confidential discussion, please contact Emilia Rodriguez on 0497 938 177 or emilia@levyl.com.au.

Levyl encourages diverse, equitable and inclusive recruitment solutions and is committed to responding to every applicant. We make selection and shortlist decisions based on your skills, experience, personal attributes and motivators. When applying for one of our advertised opportunities, please share the pronouns you use and any reasonable adjustments you may require throughout the interview process.

job.title: Talent Acquisition Partner $130-$140K + Super!
job.description:
The Organisation

Levyl is partnering with a scaling Australian financial services organisation to appoint a Talent Partner who will play a key role in supporting the next stage of growth!

The organisation has built a strong position within its market and continues to scale, with ambitious plans to expand its team across Australia. As part of this growth journey, they are investing in their internal Talent capability and looking for someone who can help build a more proactive, scalable and commercially aligned approach to recruitment.

This is an opportunity to join a business where you can genuinely see the impact of your work. You will be close to decision-making, partnering with leaders across the organisation and helping shape how great talent is attracted, engaged and hired.

The Team

Reporting to the Head of People, you will sit at the centre of the organisation’s growth strategy, partnering closely with leaders across Sales and Operations.
These teams represent the largest and most commercial areas of the business, making this a highly impactful role where your work will directly influence the organisation’s ability to grow.

You will work with leaders who are commercially driven, energetic and focused on building high-performing teams. This role will require someone who can build trust quickly, understand different personalities and confidently influence outcomes.

You will not just sit alongside the business. You will become embedded within it, understanding what makes people successful and helping leaders attract the talent they need to continue growing.

The Opportunity

As Talent Partner, you will own the hiring engine for the business, with a particular focus on Sales and Operations recruitment. You will be responsible for building always-on talent pipelines, creating exceptional candidate experiences and helping leaders make better hiring decisions. You will also take ownership of managing agency partnerships and helping to build a PSA.

This role involves managing end-to-end recruitment across a range of roles including Sales Associates, Business Development Managers, Account Executives, Team Leaders, Loan Specialists, Underwriters, Credit Operations, Customer Care, Collections and Fraud Operations as well as others across the business as needed.

Key responsibilities will include:
  • Owning end-to-end recruitment processes across Sales and Operations, from role briefing through to offer
  • Building proactive talent pipelines across key hiring areas rather than relying solely on inbound applications
  • Developing creative sourcing strategies through direct sourcing, referrals, networks and early careers channels
  • Supporting graduate and early-career hiring initiatives, including campus attraction and talent pipelines
  • Partnering closely with hiring managers to understand capability requirements and provide market insight
  • Coaching leaders through structured interviews, assessment and decision-making
  • Improving recruitment processes, systems and ways of working to create a seamless hiring experience
  • Acting as a trusted advisor to leaders, providing challenge and guidance throughout the hiring process
  • Managing external agency relationships, including preferred suppliers, recruitment briefs and partner performance
  • Helping determine when agency support is required and ensuring external partners are aligned to business needs
  • Using recruitment data and insights to track pipeline health, time-to-fill, sourcing effectiveness and opportunities for improvement
  • Providing regular visibility of recruitment progress and key metrics to senior leadership
You will also play a key role in ensuring every candidate interaction reflects the organisation positively. As the “Chief of First Impressions”, you will ensure candidates walk away with a strong view of the business, whether they are hired or not.

About You

Levyl is looking for a Talent Partner who thrives in fast-paced, evolving environments and enjoys building something meaningful.

You may come from an internal Talent Acquisition background, agency recruitment environment or a combination of both. What matters most is your ability to understand Sales and Operations talent, build strong stakeholder relationships and deliver exceptional recruitment outcomes.

You will be someone who is comfortable rolling up your sleeves, challenging thinking and finding solutions when there is no perfect playbook.

Most importantly, you will be someone candidates remember for the right reasons! You understand that every interaction shapes how people view the organisation and that great recruitment is about creating a positive experience from first contact through to offer.

The Process

This opportunity is being managed confidentially by Levyl. The interview process will include an initial conversation with Levyl, followed by three meetings with key business stakeholders, and some testing to assess how the team can support you to perform at your best! All interviews will be conducted face-to-face, in the offices.

For a confidential discussion, please contact Emilia Rodriguez from Levyl on 0497938177 or emilia@levyl.com.au

Levyl encourages diverse, equitable and inclusive recruitment solutions and is committed to responding to every applicant. We make selection and shortlist decisions based on your skills, experience, personal attributes and motivators.
